title: Defensive Compactness (Narrow Shape)
content: Defensive compactness maintains a tight, narrow defensive block that protects the central channels and forces the opponent to play wide. The team keeps short distances between all players — typically less than 25m horizontally and 30m vertically between the midfield and defensive lines. When the opponent plays wide, the block shifts laterally as a unit but does not stretch, maintaining its compact shape. The narrow block is designed to deny dangerous central passes and shots, conceding crosses from wide positions as a calculated risk. Modern compact defences rely on two key movements: (1) collective lateral shift when ball goes wide, and (2) collective forward press when ball goes backwards. Vulnerability: opposite flank switches of play that can find attackers before the block can shift across.
